quote: """Embed facts whose ``embedding`` is still NULL, in bounded batches.
why: Online fill: run() pulls one bounded page at a time (`limit=self._batch_size`, backfill.py:52-54; default 100 from the CLI) and writes each page as per-row UPDATEs on the CLI's own asyncpg connection (repository.py:415-420) - no transaction spanning the run, no DDL, no table lock - so concurrent readers and writers of `facts` are never blocked. The selected population is exactly the brief's predicate (`WHERE embedding IS NULL AND retracted_at IS NULL`, repository.py:388-389), served by the partial index idx_facts_embedding_null from migrations/009_embeddings.sql:17-18. Both texts are covered: `text = fact.natural_lang_repr or fact.symbolic_repr` (backfill.py:63) goes through `await self._llm_client.embed(text)` (72). Executed: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/memory/test_backfill.py tests/unit/test_cli_backfill.py tests/memory/test_fact_repository.py -q` -> 31 passed in 0.86s. The only blocking step is the opt-in --reindex, covered under AC-4.

quote: The repository's null predicate is the idempotency guarantee: a second run
why: Idempotency is the SQL predicate, not runner bookkeeping: `WHERE embedding IS NULL AND retracted_at IS NULL` (repository.py:388) means an already-embedded row is never selected again, while rows that failed stay null and are retried. Tests: test_second_run_only_sees_still_null_rows (tests/memory/test_backfill.py:212) runs the same runner twice over a repository that removes written rows from its null set and asserts the second run is BackfillStats(scanned=0, updated=0, failed=0) with exactly one backfill call; test_list_missing_embeddings_uses_null_predicate_and_keyset (tests/memory/test_fact_repository.py:298) asserts `embedding IS NULL` and `retracted_at IS NULL` are in the emitted SQL, so dropping the predicate would fail. Caveat, not an AC failure: a run cannot be a one-shot for rows written while it pages - store-time embedding can fail and leave NULL (fact_store.py:89) - and the interface docstring's claim about those rows is wrong (see STD-3); a rerun fills them.

Per-fact isolation: the provider call is wrapped in try/except Exception, logs the fact id and the error, increments stats.failed and continues (backfill.py:71-76); the rest of the batch is written in one call and the cursor advances even when every embed failed (`after_id = facts[-1].id` before the short-page break, backfill.py:84-88), so an outage cannot loop over the same page forever. Tests: test_partial_provider_failure_still_backfills_the_rest (test_backfill.py:154) asserts only the healthy pair is written and stats are (scanned=2, updated=1, failed=1); test_all_failed_batch_advances_the_cursor_and_terminates (170) asserts list_calls == [(2, None), (2, second)] and no backfill call. The CLI reports the count in its summary line (cli.py:310) and exits 0. Advisory: the write path sits outside this try, so a DB write error aborts the run (STD-3), and cli.py:301 builds an unwrapped client (`LLMClientFactory(settings.llm).create()`) with no breaker/pacing - consistent with main.py:194, but a provider outage then costs one failed API call per row before the table is exhausted.

Both halves are present. Default path: when anything was written the command prints the operator instruction (cli.py:313-315). Opt-in path: --reindex executes the statement exactly once, after all batches and before the connection closes (cli.py:305-308), then prints 'reindexed idx_facts_embedding' instead of the reminder; test_reindex_flag_rebuilds_the_index_after_a_write (tests/unit/test_cli_backfill.py:142) asserts conn.execute was awaited with exactly `REINDEX INDEX idx_facts_embedding` and the reminder is absent, and test_reindex_is_skipped_when_nothing_was_updated (154) pins the updated>0 guard. The statement matches migrations/009_embeddings.sql:11-12 verbatim (`REINDEX INDEX idx_facts_embedding;`), so the documented requirement is respected. Advisory (locking): REINDEX INDEX without CONCURRENTLY takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `facts` for the rebuild, so on a large table --reindex stops all reads/writes - the fill is online, this step is not; `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_facts_embedding` is legal on the pg16 image and on this autocommit connection and would keep the AC-1 no-downtime property. Advisory (silent no-op): with --reindex and updated == 0 nothing is executed and nothing is said (cli.py:305, 311), even if an earlier aborted run left the index stale.

Coverage is real and runs. test_backfill.py: batch + text selection + id/vector alignment (104), keyset pagination and cursor advance (130), partial provider failure (154), all-failed full batch terminates (170), empty table (188), empty text reported failed without a provider call (199), second-run idempotency over a mutable null set (212), batch_size < 1 rejected (228). test_fact_repository.py: null/retracted/keyset SQL and $1/$2 binding (298), explicit after_id (323), session_factory seam (335). test_cli_backfill.py: counts + reminder (99), wiring of --batch-size/client/repository (116), --db-url (131), --reindex (142), skip when nothing updated (154), no reminder on an empty run (167), batch-size validation (177), LLM construction failure exits non-zero (186). Executed: the three files -> '31 passed in 0.86s'; full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q` -> '1371 passed, 32 skipped'. Gap (non-blocking): no test of a write failure inside backfill_embeddings - the partial-failure test covers embed() raising only - so the accounting defect recorded under STD-3 is untested.

Follows the rules:list / traces:cleanup shape: nested `async def run()` under `asyncio.run(run())` (cli.py:294, 318), direct `asyncpg.connect` on the command's own connection (298), the `_connection(conn)` adapter passed as session_factory (300; the same seam as rules:list cli.py:155-158 and rules:archive 256), Typer options with help text and `min=1` on --batch-size (275-280), and typer.echo output (310-315); the connection is closed in a finally even when the runner raises. Two advisory deviations: (1) it inlines `db_url or settings.database.database_url` instead of the `_database_url(db_url)` helper used by the other new commands - equivalent here because settings must be loaded anyway for the llm slice, and the `or` short-circuit means --db-url still wins without touching the database slice; (2) the operator reminder is `run REINDEX INDEX idx_facts_embedding; after a large backfill` (315), a leftover semicolon from the migration sentence that reads as a typo, and tests/unit/test_cli_backfill.py:112 asserts it verbatim, so the wording is now pinned - worth fixing once.

quote: return self._session_factory() if self._session_factory is not None else DbSession()
why: `PostgresFactRepository` gains the same injectable seam as `PostgresRuleRepository` (rules/repository.py:30-33): an optional session_factory plus a `_session()` helper, and all 12 pre-existing methods plus the new one go through it (the diff removes 12 `async with DbSession() as db:` lines and adds 13 `async with self._session() as db:`). The default resolves at call time inside `_session()` (line 60), not at class-definition time, so `patch('cortex.memory.repository.DbSession')` still intercepts every method: the pre-existing fixtures at tests/memory/test_fact_repository.py:64, 180, 247, 295 and tests/memory/test_semantic_search.py:80 patch it on a no-arg repository and pass. The CLI injects `_connection(conn)` (cli.py:300), so --db-url is honoured without the shared pool. Every production caller passes no argument (main.py:180), so the new optional parameter is backward compatible. `PostgresConceptRepository` (repository.py:441) is untouched by the diff. Executed: `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check` on the changed files -> 'All checks passed!'; `.venv/bin/python -m mypy src/cortex/memory/backfill.py src/cortex/memory/repository.py src/cortex/cli.py` -> 'Success: no issues found in 3 source files'.

quote: The keyset cursor (``id > after_id``) lets a caller page without
why: The SQL, parameter order, alignment and cursor advance are right: `WHERE embedding IS NULL AND retracted_at IS NULL / AND ($2::uuid IS NULL OR id > $2::uuid) / ORDER BY id / LIMIT $1` (repository.py:388-394) is called with (limit, after_id) so $1=limit and $2=after_id bind as intended; ids and vectors are appended only for successes and zipped `strict=True` after the length check (backfill.py:77-78, repository.py:409-420); the cursor is set from `facts[-1].id` before the short-page break (backfill.py:86-88), so an all-failed batch cannot loop forever. Two defects. (1) The new interface docstring is false: 'The keyset cursor (``id > after_id``) lets a caller page without skipping rows that were written between two queries.' (interfaces.py:224-225) - facts.id defaults to `gen_random_uuid()` (migrations/003_facts.sql:5), a v4 id, and store() does not supply one (repository.py:64-70), so a fact written while the run is paging can sort behind the cursor and is invisible to that run; probe: take two sorted v4 ids, set the cursor to the high one, the later-inserted low id is not returned by the next page (printed False). Safe in the end - the row stays NULL and the next run fills it - but the documented contract as written is wrong; either say 'does not skip rows whose id sorts after the cursor; rows written behind it need a follow-up run' or drop the sentence. (2) `stats.updated += len(ids)` (backfill.py:82) runs only after `backfill_embeddings` returns, and that method issues one autocommitted UPDATE per pair with no transaction (`async with self._session() as db:` / `for fact_id, embedding in zip(fact_ids, embeddings, strict=True):` / `await db.execute('UPDATE facts SET embedding = $2::vector WHERE id = $1')`, repository.py:415-420). A failure mid-batch - e.g. a provider returning a 3072-dim vector into vector(1536) - leaves the earlier UPDATEs durable, skips the counter, and propagates out of run(); the CLI then prints no counts and skips the REINDEX reminder. Probe with a 3-fact batch failing on write #2: 'run aborted with: ValueError expected 1536 dimensions, not 3072', 'durably written before abort: 1', stats never returned. Not fatal: written rows are correct, the null predicate makes a rerun skip them, and the operator sees a crash rather than a false success - but the counts the command exists to print do not match durable state, and one malformed vector kills the whole run. Fix: wrap each batch in `db.transaction()` (or use executemany) and add len(ids) to stats.updated only after the commit; the runner docstring line 29 ('A batch is written as one ``backfill_embeddings`` call') makes it look atomic when it is not.

Docs: architecture.md's CLI inventory - the only place that lists commands - now includes the new command on the same paragraph as token:create / traces:cleanup / rules:*. ADR-0008's decision is 'embeddings are generated eagerly at store_fact() time'; the backfill closes exactly the rows written before that path existed, which the module docstring states (`"""Backfill embeddings for facts written before the provider existed (ADR-0008, #159)."""`, backfill.py:1) and the null-embedding query implements. The REINDEX requirement from migrations/009_embeddings.sql:11-12 ('after a large backfill, run REINDEX INDEX idx_facts_embedding;') is respected twice over: the backfill_embeddings docstring repeats it (repository.py:405-407) and the CLI both reminds the operator and can perform it (cli.py:306, 315). Advisory: ADR-0008 itself still reads as if every fact is embedded at write time and never mentions the backfill or the NULL left by a failed store-time embed; one sentence there would keep the ADR accurate, though no acceptance criterion or deliverable requires editing it.

Both STD-3 defects are fixed. (1) Atomicity/accounting: `backfill_embeddings` now wraps the whole batch in one `async with db.transaction():` around the UPDATE loop (repository.py:417-423), and `stats.updated += len(ids)` (backfill.py:82) still runs only after that call returns, i.e. after the commit - so a mid-batch failure rolls the batch back, writes nothing durable, never touches the counter, and propagates. That is the truthful behaviour my previous row asked for; the runner now pins the propagation (test_backfill_write_failure_propagates, tests/memory/test_backfill.py:180) and the repository pins the ordering (test_backfill_wraps_every_update_in_one_transaction, tests/memory/test_fact_repository.py:272: begin, update, update, commit). (2) The false cursor claim is gone: the interface now says 'The keyset cursor (``id > after_id``) avoids the offset drift of ``LIMIT/OFFSET`` while rows are being written. A fact inserted with an id below the cursor is not seen by the current run; a later run's null predicate picks it up.' (interfaces.py:224-227), which matches gen_random_uuid() v4 ids and is the accurate contract. (3) The locking advisory moved to AC-4 and is fixed there. Executed (my own, not the fixer's numbers): live pgvector/pg16 container on 127.0.0.1:55432 - raw `cortex.cli._connection` adapter, batch of 2 with one 3-dim vector -> DataError 'expected 1536 dimensions, not 3', then 2/2 rows still NULL; one-row retry -> 1 NULL. Pooled `DbSession` with cortex.db.pool._pool monkeypatched to a real asyncpg pool, batch of 2 with one bad vector -> DataError, 2/2 rows still NULL; one-row retry -> 1 NULL. So rollback holds on both session surfaces and a clean batch commits. `pytest tests -q` -> 1374 passed, 32 skipped; the four touched test files -> 39 passed; ruff and mypy on the changed files -> clean. Residual advisory: the committed repository test mocks `__aexit__`/`__aenter__`, so rollback-on-exception itself is not asserted in CI and the live check is not committed - acceptable in a repo with no DB-backed suite, but worth remembering if `DbSession.transaction()` is ever edited.

The locking advisory is resolved: `--reindex` now runs `REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_facts_embedding` instead of the ACCESS-EXCLUSIVE form, so the explicit rebuild no longer blocks readers/writers and AC-1's no-downtime property holds for the flag too. Placement is correct: the statement executes after `EmbeddingBackfillRunner(...).run()` returns (cli.py:303-307), i.e. after every per-batch transaction has committed, and outside any explicit transaction - `conn` is a bare asyncpg connection in autocommit. Measured on the live pgvector/pg16 container: the same statement on a raw asyncpg connection -> OK, including immediately after the batch; the same statement inside `async with conn.transaction():` -> ActiveSQLTransactionError 'REINDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block', which proves the CLI's placement is the only valid one and that a future move inside the runner's transaction would fail loudly. The `updated == 0` skip is gone (`if reindex:`, cli.py:306), covered by test_reindex_runs_even_when_nothing_was_updated (tests/unit/test_cli_backfill.py:160) - the stale-index-after-aborted-run case is real even with atomic batches, because a run can abort after earlier batches committed. The reminder is now 'run REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_facts_embedding after a large backfill' (cli.py:316) with the stray semicolon gone, and migrations/009_embeddings.sql:12 was updated to the same CONCURRENTLY instruction, so CLI, repository docstring and migration agree. Residual advisory (not new): if the concurrent rebuild itself fails, the exception propagates before the counts are printed (pre-existing shape), and REINDEX CONCURRENTLY needs index ownership plus roughly 2x index space - operational notes only.
